title: Choir and Thorn
premise: Beatrix Vasquez, a cartographer of unmapped realms, has spent twelve years selling small charms in Grayhollow, a city that outlawed magic, hiding her gift behind ink and silence. When a dying stranger presses a living map into her hands and dies whispering her true name, she discovers the map is the last dragon-fire's memory — and that her own soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain long ago. To reclaim it, she must gather a ragged found family: a disgraced choir-singer whose voice opens doors between worlds, a thief who owes the stranger his life, and the stranger's ghost, who refuses to leave. In the court beneath the mountain, Beatrix learns the price of belonging: she can keep her soul only by giving up the map — and with it, every unmapped realm she has ever loved. She chooses instead to redraw the bargain itself, burning the map's final page to free the dragon-fire, restore her soul, and carry her new family home to a city that will finally have to make room for magic.
about_author: Juniper Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people who build families out of strangers, secrets, and stubborn hope.

chapters.title: The Dying Cartographer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In Grayhollow's night market, Beatrix sells harmless charms while hiding her cartographer's gift from the Wardens. A bleeding stranger finds her stall, presses a folded map into her hands, whispers her childhood name, and dies. The map is warm, alive, and humming. Emotional beat: fear and recognition — her buried past has found her.

chapters.title: Ink That Breathes
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Hiding in her attic workshop, she unrolls the map and watches it redraw itself, showing a road beneath the mountain and a cell where something soul-shaped is kept. The stranger's ghost appears, unable to speak but able to point. Wardens raid the street below. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve — she cannot unknow what the map shows.

chapters.title: A Voice for Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera Vane, once the celebrated singer of the Warden's own choir, now sings in taverns for coppers, her voice banned after it cracked open a sealed door three years ago. Beatrix buys her a drink and asks for one song at the mountain's gate. Sera refuses — then hears the map hum her mother's lullaby. Emotional beat: longing for a purpose worth the risk.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Owes a Ghost
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Pickpocket Dov Fen recognizes the dead stranger as the man who once bought his freedom from a debt-broker. When Beatrix comes asking about him, Dov agrees to guide them through the undercity tunnels — partly for the ghost, mostly because he's tired of owing. Emotional beat: guilt transmuting into loyalty; the trio becomes a company.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The Wardens torch the charm-market hunting the map, and Beatrix watches twelve years of careful anonymity go up in smoke. The ghost leads them through burning alleys to the old tram tunnel. Sera sings a wall open for the first time since her disgrace. Emotional beat: grief for the safe small life, and the first taste of chosen family.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. In the unmapped dark, the map feeds on Beatrix's memories to draw their way forward, taking her recollections of her sister with each mile. Dov realizes what it costs her and starts lying about the route to spare her. The ghost grows fainter the deeper they go. Emotional beat: tenderness and sacrifice — love measured in what you refuse to let someone pay alone.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They reach the underground court, beautiful and wrong, where the Grieving King keeps souls in glass lanterns to light his endless dusk. Sera's singing buys them an audience; the King offers Beatrix her soul back in exchange for the map. She sees her own childhood self flickering inside a lantern. Emotional beat: seduction and horror — the temptation to trade the future for the past.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Held in the court while the King waits, Beatrix relives why she sold her soul at nineteen: to buy her dying sister one more year, believing magic always demands a price. The ghost finally speaks — he was the broker who took it, and he has been trying to give it back ever since. Emotional beat: shame met with forgiveness; the past reframed.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Dov and Sera's POV (alternating). While the King sleeps, they steal into the lantern vault where the last dragon-fire gutters, keeping all the court's bargains alight. Sera sings the fire awake; Dov shatters the lantern holding Beatrix's soul. The court begins to collapse as every old bargain unravels at once. Emotional beat: desperate courage — the climax ignites.

chapters.title: A Map With Room in It
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Offered escape through any door the map can draw, Beatrix instead tears out its final page and feeds it to the freed dragon-fire, ending the economy of souls forever. The ghost fades smiling; the company climbs toward dawn over Grayhollow, where small charms are beginning to glow openly in windows. Emotional beat: belonging earned — not a place on the map, but people to share it with.
